Election results revealed regional divides across California, with wealthy Bay Area enclaves Marin County and San Mateo County voting against Prop 40. However, 55% of San Francisco County voters favored the measure, reflecting a stark geographic split.

Opponents simultaneously promoted competing ballot measures designed to nullify wealth taxes , with Prop 42 leading in early vote tallies. That measure would prohibit taxes on personal savings, assets, and retirement holdings.

The university awaits an independent review led by former U.S. Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates, while New York Attorney General Letitia James oversees a separate criminal investigation into the 2024 allegations.

Resources are being redirected toward the Cybercab, a two-seat robotaxi central to Tesla's autonomous-vehicle strategy, with approximately 570 units operating among more than 1,200 robotaxis in Texas according to Texas DMV figures.

Production at the Texas facility will wind down around June or July next year, while Tesla vice president of vehicle engineering Lars Moravy intends to begin selling Cybercabs to customers by year-end 2026.
title: Tesla to add Cybertruck shift to clear orders before dismantling line next year

Spearheaded by Stephen Miller, the new White House Chief of Staff, the administration's campaign to penalize nonprofits follows Miller's earlier vow to "dismantle and take on the radical left organizations" in the country.
The plan hinges on Section 501 of the tax code, a provision that has never been tested in this way. It would bypass standard IRS audits and court access, allowing unilateral suspension of exemptions.

Though the administration signaled interest in targeting groups like the Southern Poverty Law Center and the Council on American-Islamic Relations , White House officials characterized the potential order as "speculative," leaving the full scope unclear.

With only 32 active astronauts, NASA needs more recruits to expand humanity's presence beyond Earth as quickly as possible, following the agency's last call for new astronauts two years ago.

Artemis III commander Randy Bresnik urged potential candidates not to delay, saying "We're going to have people on the moon." Frank Rubio, who holds a U.S. endurance record with 371 consecutive days in space, emphasized that patience is essential.

NASA expects to make its final selection by late 2027. Officials noted that while candidates contribute to the mission of going to the moon, that will be about 1% of their experience, as most work occurs closer to Earth.

Candidates will support Artemis missions, including efforts to land astronauts near the lunar south pole. Future training involves practicing docking capsules with lunar landers built by Elon Musk's SpaceX and Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin.
title: NASA Opens Applications for New Astronaut Class to Expand Artemis

bias: Left-Leaning coverage personalizes the proposed inquiry around Trump, using charged phrases such as “puts the hammer down,” “lied,” and “nasty surprise,” while emphasizing possible misconduct by lawyers or officials.
Right-Leaning coverage de-emphasizes those implications and gives the procedural question—whether the government “misled” the court—less elaboration.
Center coverage sits between them, stressing Judge Ana Reyes’s proposed appointment of Jessie K.
Liu and describing the renovation as Trump’s “prized” project.
The pivotal divide is whether the episode is portrayed chiefly as a Trump-linked setback or as a conditional investigation into litigation conduct; all accounts agree on the proposed inquiry.
summary: On Saturday, U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes announced her intent to appoint Jessie Liu as Special Master to investigate whether administration lawyers misled the court regarding the East Potomac Golf Course renovation.

Reyes has been pressing administration lawyers, seeking to determine if Department of Justice and Interior Department officials provided truthful information about construction plans, including the controversial tree-cutting events from last month.

President Donald Trump 's Truth Social posts indicated plans to close the park on November 15 for 15 months, contradicting earlier assurances from Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward that no such closure was planned.

Legal experts suggest the initiation of a formal investigation 'can be a precursor to holding someone in contempt of court,' as Liu examines whether officials violated ethics rules in their dealings with the court.
Both sides must submit any objections to the appointment of Liu in writing by Friday, November 13, as the court continues the lawsuit initiated by the District of Columbia Preservation League.
title: Judge wants former US attorney to investigate whether the government misled her in Trump golf case

bias: Left-Leaning coverage emphasizes institutional context—his brief NYPD service and school-aide role—while framing the “apparently random” attack and landfill search as investigative concerns; terms like “fatal slashing” and “covered in blood” add drama.

Right-Leaning coverage foregrounds law-and-order fear, highlighting alleged admissions, the neck wound, memory-loss claims, and psychological background, with labels such as “maniac,” “brutally murdered,” and “emotionless” encouraging moral condemnation.

Center coverage stays comparatively restrained, using “suspect” and “charged.” All perspectives converge on Suarez’s death, the second-degree-murder charge, and the suspect’s arrest, while diverging over institutional accountability versus punishment, danger, and cultural anxieties about public safety.
summary: On Saturday, the NYPD arrested Sayed Mohassib, 27, a Department of Education employee and former police officer, charging him with second-degree murder in the October 30 stabbing death of Brooklyn jogger Katie Suarez, 28.

Suarez was attacked while running along the Shore Parkway Greenway in Bath Beach on October 30, with investigators characterizing the fatal stabbing as a random, unprovoked incident that occurred shortly after she spoke with her father by phone.
Surveillance footage from near the path helped detectives track Mohassib, who reportedly told officers he could not recall the attack but claimed he woke up covered in blood while carrying a knife.
Following the death, community members held vigils for Suarez, with local officials demanding increased patrols, security cameras, and lighting along the remote waterfront path to improve safety.
Investigators are continuing their search for the suspected murder weapon, with authorities scouring a sanitation barge in New Jersey and reviewing dashcam footage from the evening of the attack.
title: School aide who briefly served as NYPD officer arrested in fatal stabbing of Brooklyn jogger

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames four of eight appointees retaining drug stocks as “financial conflicts” on a “powerful” panel whose recommendations can shape insurers’ required coverage, stressing ethics and public trust.

Right-Leaning coverage emphasizes officials’ ability to retain pharmaceutical interests and portrays “exemptions” as troubling exceptions, reflecting skepticism toward government health institutions and industry ties.
Center coverage uses “own” and “influential,” describing investments and waivers with less interpretive force.
The pivotal divide is whether waivers resolve or merely expose conflicts.
All perspectives highlight the four-to-eight ratio, investments, and panel authority, revealing a broader tension over regulatory accountability and institutional trust.
summary: Four of the eight members appointed by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to the United States Preventive Services Task Force retain stock in companies affected by the panel's decisions, according to conflict-of-interest waivers.

Historically, the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality required task force candidates to sell pharmaceutical stocks, but new waivers now permit members to maintain investments in firms like Eli Lilly and Pfizer.

Dr. Patrick K. Hunter and Dr. Ronald P. Karlsberg hold pharmaceutical stocks, with AHRQ director Dr. Roger D. Klein arguing each member individually has "no power to render a final decision on behalf of the United States."
Former AHRQ scientific director Dr. Quyen Ngo-Metzger stated that such industry involvement "undermines the trust in the process," arguing candidates should divest to maintain public confidence.

Department of Health and Human Services spokesperson Emily Hilliard said Supreme Court rulings defining members as "special government employees" necessitate these waivers, which federal law provides as an "appropriate remedy" for conflicts.
title: Four Top RFK Appointees Allowed To Keep Drug Stocks
topic_full: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. · United States

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Katz’s remarks around immediate peril—“threatens,” “real danger,” an unfinished “mission”—while highlighting his warning to Hezbollah and the backdrop of possible Israeli political change.

Right-Leaning coverage sharpens the adversarial narrative by foregrounding Iran’s alleged “renewing” pursuit of “nuclear weapons ,” pairing “warns” with calls for “national unity” and military readiness, while noting Iran’s denial.
The pivotal divide is whether the story centers regional escalation and domestic politics or an existential nuclear threat warranting continued action.
Both perspectives portray Iran as dangerous and Israel’s mission as incomplete, reflecting broader disputes over intervention, security priorities, and political leadership.
summary: Defense Minister Israel Katz warned that Iran is reviving its pursuit of nuclear weapons during a memorial service for Operation Kadesh soldiers, urging Israelis to prioritize national security over internal divisions.

Regarding Iran, Katz stated "the mission is not yet complete," emphasizing that Israel must pursue a proactive, offensive policy to counter threats from Tehran while protecting citizens through necessary action.

The Defense Ministry and Elbit signed a deal investing over $190M in artillery training, reinforcing that public support for the Israel Defense Forces signals to enemies that domestic disagreements do not weaken national resolve.

"We have one country, one military, and a shared destiny," Katz stated, arguing that while public debate is acceptable, national security requires rising above internal differences when the nation faces external threats.

He concluded by calling for "unity, responsibility and mutual commitment," emphasizing that future challenges require combining the strength of the Israel Defense Forces with the resilience of the public.
title: Israel Says Iran Mission ‘Not Complete’: ‘They’re Trying to Get Nuclear Weapons'

bias: Coverage converges on Abdul El-Sayed ’s opposition to U.S. support for Israel and willingness to work with Trump, but diverges in emphasis: left-leaning framing highlights his “praises” of a reported $4 billion cut and cross-party cooperation; center coverage presents “rare common ground” while adding his broader call to end aid and ban weapons sales, plus his distinction between Judaism and Israel; right-leaning framing foregrounds “subsidize a foreign military,” “awful things,” and weapons allegedly used harmfully.
The pivotal divide is whether this is pragmatic cooperation, expanded policy, or moral condemnation—though all stress reducing U.S. military support.
summary: On Tuesday, President Donald Trump announced plans to end approximately $4 billion in annual United States military aid to Israel by the end of 2026, citing an earlier agreement with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed welcomed the decision during an appearance on Thursday's Morning Joe, stating, "I think the president is actually right on this policy."

El-Sayed, the first Muslim American elected to the Senate, called for halting American arms sales to Israel, arguing taxpayer dollars should not fund actions he described as "genocide" and "apartheid" in Gaza and the West Bank.

The Democrat rejected claims that criticizing Israel constitutes antisemitism, emphasizing the need to separate Judaism from Israeli government policies while affirming commitment to Jewish children's safety.
El-Sayed advocated for a broader review of military support for Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Pakistan, arguing American taxpayer dollars should be prioritized for domestic needs instead.
title: El-Sayed backs Trump plan to end Israel aid: ‘I agree with him on that’

summary: On Monday, the Crown withdrew all criminal charges against 44 pro-Palestinian protesters arrested during an April 2024 sit-in at a downtown Montreal Scotiabank, officially ending the prosecution.
Protesters occupied the branch demanding Scotiabank divest from Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit Systems, a move the bank eventually completed, which activists welcomed as a victory.

While 14 individuals previously pleaded guilty to municipal noise bylaw violations and paid $300 fines, defense lawyer Barbara Bedont noted most other protesters resolved their cases through community service.
Defendants challenged the charges under the Charter, arguing police violated their rights, and filed a formal complaint against the presiding judge alleging bias and unfair treatment.
Defense counsel Bedont warned that criminalizing peaceful sit-ins threatens the right to protest, suggesting the group's legal strategy likely influenced the Crown's decision to drop charges.
title: No Criminal Charges for Montreal Protesters Arrested at Bank Sit-In

summary: Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Anthony Santander shared Islamophobic videos on his Instagram Story following Tuesday's U.S. elections, sparking widespread online outrage and criticism from fans.

One video from The American Truth Project claimed elected Muslim politicians are radicals seeking to impose Sharia law; a Christian minister in a separate clip described Islam as "violent" and "driven by war."

A Blue Jays spokesperson addressed the controversy, stating, "Individual comments do not represent our organization's values and beliefs," while emphasizing the club's commitment to inclusivity for all fans.
Santander, a 32-year-old Venezuelan who signed a $92.5 million contract ahead of 2025, missed the entire 2026 season following shoulder surgery after appearing in only 54 games.
Although the player deleted the content after receiving backlash, screenshots of the posts went viral on social media, drawing sustained criticism from fans who called the rhetoric harmful.
title: Blue Jays say RF Anthony Santander’s anti-Muslim posts do not represent the team’s values

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Medicare for All as a popular mandate, urging Democrats to “let’s pass” it and portraying Sanders as “on a roll,” while casting his interruption as being “brought back down to earth.” Right-leaning coverage stresses political uncertainty—“could pass,” “not absolutely certain,” and “veto”—and depicts the plan as “government-funded” expansion, including possible eligibility at 55 and broader benefits.
The pivotal divide is whether public support—over 60% overall and 80–90% among Democrats—justifies action or whether costs, federal reach, and feasibility warrant skepticism.
Center coverage emphasizes Democrats’ “major changes” after electoral gains.
All agree Sanders advocated universal coverage, exposing broader disputes over government’s role.
summary: On Thursday, Sen. Bernie Sanders urged Democrats to pass Medicare for All legislation, arguing the party must deliver on the healthcare mandate voters provided during Tuesday's midterm elections.
Following a sweeping midterm victory, progressives view the Democratic landslide as evidence that voters demand significant change, with 66% of Americans supporting Medicare for All.
Sanders argued the party must prioritize repealing $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts and restoring Affordable Care Act tax credits, while lowering the Medicare eligibility age to 55.
While President Donald Trump holds veto power, Sanders challenged Democrats to pass the legislation anyway, suggesting the popular policy might not prompt a presidential rejection.
Sanders plans to utilize the reconciliation process, which requires only 51 votes in the Senate, as he prepares to chair the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee.
title: Sanders Calls for Democrats to Pass ‘Medicare for All’

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Trump’s defeat as deserved and self-inflicted, using terms such as “Dirty,” “thrashed,” and “savaged,” while broadening the story to Kemi Badenoch ’s criticism of Boris Johnson and Liz Truss.
Right-Leaning coverage de-emphasizes that wider context, stressing the scale of the “thrashing” as an intra-conservative critique.
Center coverage links the Republican loss to Trump’s political style and invokes a possible “beginning of the end,” with “slams” and “brutal dig” heightening drama.
Across perspectives, Badenoch—the UK Conservative Party leader—is reported as saying Trump deserved defeat, revealing shared emphasis amid differing judgments about its cause and significance.
summary: On Saturday, Kemi Badenoch , of the Conservative Party, criticized President Donald Trump following Republican losses in the United States midterm elections, calling the defeat "entirely self-inflicted."
Badenoch claimed the President's focus on himself rather than voters caused the loss, arguing Americans voted against his arrogance rather than the Republican Party.
In a sweeping critique, Badenoch attacked Trump's record on foreign policy, slamming his approach to the Iran War, threats toward Canada and Greenland, and tariffs harming cost of living.
Branding Trump's treatment of Volodymyr Zelensky in the White House "awful," Badenoch condemned his "dirty" style of politics and insisted politicians avoid "squabbling with allies" like Britain.
The Conservative Party has learned from Trump's loss, according to Badenoch, who explained that a party cannot win if it only talks to its base, rejecting "gimmicks, mistakes and short-termism.
title: ‘Dirty’ Trump deserved to be thrashed in the US midterms, says Kemi Badenoch

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the midterms through “human rights,” spotlighting Virginia’s rights-restoration measure and treating ballot politics as civil-rights stakes.

Center coverage narrows attention to “anti-trans” measures approved in four states, calling them a “warning” and a “challenge” for Democrats while tempering predictions with the “blue wave” question and historical caution about 2028.

Right-Leaning coverage similarly emphasizes Democratic vulnerability but adds partisan context, portraying attacks on Democrats as “overly liberal” on transgender athletes and gender-affirming care, and highlighting that these measures passed despite a nationwide Democratic win.
All perspectives recognize socially contested ballot measures and their electoral significance, reflecting broader disputes over rights, party strategy, and cultural politics.
summary: Voters in Washington, Colorado, Arizona, and Nebraska approved ballot measures on Tuesday restricting transgender rights, signaling a political challenge for Democrats heading into the 2028 presidential race.

Republicans wielded anti-transgender messaging effectively in midterm campaigns, attacking opponents as overly liberal on sports participation and gender-affirming care, while Democrats responded with mixed strategies from conservative postures to pro-transgender positions.

A Reuters/Ipsos poll found 67% of survey respondents supported banning transgender people from competing in female school sports; ninety-two percent of Republicans backed such bans, compared with just 44% of Democrats.

Despite the ballot measures passing, voters in Washington, Colorado, and Arizona elected Democrats to a majority of state and federal seats, while Alabama and Michigan elected transgender state lawmakers for the first time.

The success of these initiatives is "disheartening," said Rachel Tomlinson Dick, executive director of LGBTQ advocacy group Out Nebraska, as critics warn that shifting toward Republican positions risks alienating the party's progressive wing.
title: US anti-trans ballot wins pose challenge for Democrats ahead of 2028

bias: The available coverage contrasts a restrained center framing—“anti-Israel groups” planning a “boycott” of named businesses near Kristallnacht—with a right-leaning portrayal of an antisemitic campaign to expel Jewish-owned shops.

Center coverage emphasizes the promotional graphic and locations, while right coverage stresses “targeting,” official condemnation, and alleged intent, using charged terms such as “chilling,” “Jew-haters,” “must go,” and “Nazi terror.” The pivotal divide is whether the action addresses Israeli ties or Jewish identity.
Left-Leaning coverage is de-emphasized here.
Both perspectives highlight the boycott’s timing, business list, and controversy, reflecting wider disputes over Israel, antisemitism , protest tactics, and historical memory.
summary: Anti-Israel groups scheduled a " Boycott Ride" for Sunday, Nov 8, in Philadelphia's Rittenhouse Square, targeting Jewish and Israeli-owned businesses including Dizengoff, Huda, and Goldie.
Organizers set the demonstration for the eve of Kristallnacht, the 1938 Nazi-orchestrated pogrom that destroyed Jewish businesses and synagogues in Germany and Austria.
Promotional flyers from Philly Bike On Your Left feature crossed-out icons targeting Mac Mart, K'Far Cafe, and Schlesinger. Organizers demand these "Zionist establishments must go."

The Anti-Defamation League Philadelphia, American Jewish Committee Philadelphia, Jewish Federation of Greater Philadelphia, and StandWithUs condemned the campaign as "Jew-hatred, plain and simple." They urged residents to support targeted businesses.

Groups called on Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro, Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle Parker, and District Attorney Larry Krasner to condemn the event, requesting the Philadelphia Police Department ensure business safety.
title: Officials condemn planned Philadelphia boycott of Jewish-owned businesses as antisemitic

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Trump’s DOJ directive as retaliation and intimidation, using terms like “tirade,” “threatens,” and “imprisonment,” while highlighting constitutional dangers of targeting political opponents after a Democratic “blue tsunami.” Right-leaning coverage reverses the lens, portraying Democratic oversight and impeachment plans as “extortion,” “blackmail,” or actions by “extortionist Democrats” against officials and donors, making Trump’s investigation seem like a response to abuse.

The pivotal divide is whether congressional scrutiny represents legitimate oversight or coercive threats; center coverage adds that Trump offered no evidence and labels the allegations “alleged.” All acknowledge the directive, Democratic investigative plans, and a deeply polarized struggle over accountability and executive power.
summary: On Saturday, President Donald Trump ordered the Justice Department to investigate Democrats, alleging their impeachment threats against officials and donors constitute a "criminal act" without providing evidence.
In a Truth Social post, Trump accused Democrats of "extortion at the highest level," claiming they threaten respected donors with imprisonment despite admitting they lack grounds for impeachment.
Sen. Elissa Slotkin was singled out by Trump, who claimed she intends to target young people supporting Republican Values, though he offered no evidence for this allegation.
Incoming Democratic majorities in Congress prepare to launch investigations into the administration, which Trump characterized as "Weaponization and Lawfare at another level."
Asserting these "EXTORTIONISTS" should be imprisoned, Trump urged Republicans to act quickly and alleged that Democrat Political Leaders sent threatening letters to innocent people.
title: Trump orders DOJ to look into Democrats for 'threatening' people

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the claim cautiously as a “China spy” allegation attributed to U.S. intelligence, while center coverage adds “targeted” and “spy plot,” portraying an alleged operation against Jensen Huang .

Right-Leaning accounts intensify the threat frame with “top spy agency,” “recruited,” and “Chinese spy,” highlighting possible access to Huang, Nvidia’s AI-chip decisions, and speculation that Huang himself may have been targeted.

Thus, the divide is over emphasis and operational detail—not proof of influence: all describe a reported intelligence assessment, while noting no public responses from Huang, Nvidia, the woman, or Chinese authorities, and no publicly documented supporting evidence.
summary: Alice Huang, a Megaspeed International executive, was recruited as a spy for China's MSS to target Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang , according to a Trump administration memo circulated among policymakers.

Intelligence cited in the memo last spring identified Alice Huang as having a close relationship with Jensen Huang and tasked her to collect intelligence on American AI chips and potentially influence Nvidia.

Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia cloud partner, allegedly sought advanced chip intelligence while building data centers in South-east Asia for China, according to American officials briefed on the matter.
On Thursday, the House Select Committee requested a closed-door briefing with Jensen Huang regarding his interactions with Alice Huang and company security protocols, though Nvidia denies wrongdoing.

The case has intensified Capitol Hill scrutiny and debate over American chip sales to China, sharpening security concerns as Democrats gain congressional control following this week's midterm elections.
title: Chinese Spy Who Targeted Jensen Huang Worked Directly for China’s Top Spy Agency: NYT

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Rubio’s intervention as expanding “grip,” issuing a “stern warning,” and managing the “fallout” from Kimberly Guilfoyle’s resignation—suggesting power consolidation and scandal.

Right-Leaning coverage recasts the same conduct as an effort to “impose order,” stop officials “freelancing,” and deliver a “blunt message,” while linking it to midterm losses and possible 2028 ambitions.
Center coverage gives more space to allegations of access-selling, Republican distancing from an “increasingly unpopular Trump administration,” and possible travel-approval rules.
All perspectives emphasize conflicts of interest, internal discipline, and 2028, reflecting wider divides over accountability, authority, and partisan succession.
summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio directed senior staff to coordinate on all significant policy decisions, requiring signoff from him or Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau. He warned that unethical behavior would result in firing.

Recent departures, including US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle and Special Representative for Global Partnerships Paolo Zampolli, prompted this shift. Zampolli was fired in October after being accused of working outside his 'lane' of cultural diplomacy.

Policy chief Jeremy Lewin was also forced out due to concerns about 'freelancing' and defying 'certain directives from the Secretary.' Rubio now requires his office to approve all overseas political travel.

With Democrats taking control of Congress in January, investigations into the Trump administration's dealings are expected to intensify. Rubio's management of the State Department could become a focal point if he pursues a potential 2028 presidential run.

Following midterm electoral losses, top Republicans are attempting to distance themselves from the increasingly unpopular Trump administration. While Rubio has downplayed presidential ambitions, he has not publicly ruled out a campaign.
title: Rubio Seeks to Impose Order at State as Republicans Look Ahead to 2028: Report
